examples.ko: 그 사람은 고리대금업자에게 돈을 빌렸다가 크게 고생했어요.
examples.en: He borrowed money from a loan shark and suffered a lot.
The loan shark in the drama was really scary.
The news warned people to be careful of loan sharks.
I heard my grandfather worked as a moneylender when he was young.

examples.ko: 고리대금업자가 이자를 너무 높게 받아서 문제가 됐어요.
examples.en: It became a problem because the loan shark charged too much interest.

examples.ko: 급해도 고리대금업자한테는 절대 돈을 빌리지 마세요.
examples.en: Even if you are in a hurry, never borrow money from a loan shark.

explain: 일상에서는 '사채업자'라고 더 자주 말해요. '고리대금업자'는 이자를 아주 높게 받는다는 비판의 느낌이 들어서 뉴스나 이야기 속에서 많이 나와요. 보통 '고리대금업자에게 돈을 빌리다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: In daily life people more often say '사채업자' (private moneylender). '고리대금업자' carries a critical feeling that the interest is extremely high, so it often appears in news and stories. It is usually used like '고리대금업자에게 돈을 빌리다' (borrow money from a loan shark).

examples.en: As soon as I took off my shoes, a stink spread everywhere.
The socks stink, so I should wash them right away.
What is that stink in this room?
The old cheese smells terrible.

examples.ko: 운동화 속 고린내를 없애는 방법이 있어요?
examples.en: Is there a way to get rid of the stink inside sneakers?
I opened the window wide because of the stink.

explain: 발, 양말, 오래된 음식에서 나는 고약한 냄새에 많이 써요. 보통 '고린내가 나다'로 말해요. '구린내'도 비슷하게 쓰지만 방귀나 똥 같은 냄새를 더 떠올려요.
explain_en: It is used for nasty smells from feet, socks, or old food, and usually appears as '고린내가 나다'. '구린내' is similar, but it makes people think more of smells like gas or poop.

examples.ko: 정부는 외교적 고립화를 막으려고 노력하고 있어요.
examples.en: The government is trying to prevent diplomatic isolation.

examples.ko: 노인 고립화 문제가 점점 심해지고 있어요.
examples.en: The problem of elderly isolation is getting worse.

examples.ko: 도시에서 개인의 고립화가 빨라지는 것 같아요.
examples.en: It seems that individual isolation is speeding up in cities.

examples.ko: 고립화가 계속되면 마음의 병이 생길 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If isolation continues, you may develop mental health problems.

examples.ko: 마을의 고립화를 막기 위해 버스 노선을 늘렸어요.
examples.en: They added bus routes to keep the village from becoming isolated.

examples.ko: 이웃과 이야기하면 고립화를 줄일 수 있어요.
examples.en: Talking with your neighbors can reduce isolation.

explain: 뉴스나 사회 이야기에서 '고립화 현상', '고립화 문제'처럼 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '혼자가 되다', '고립되다'라고 더 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It often appears in news and social topics, as in '고립화 현상' and '고립화 문제'. In everyday talk people more often say '혼자가 되다' or '고립되다'.

examples.ko: 작년 여름에 제주도에 갔어요. 고맘때 날씨가 정말 좋았어요.
examples.en: I went to Jeju Island last summer. The weather around that time was really nice.
Kids are the cutest right around that age.
Around that age, everyone goes through puberty.
I thought like that at that age too.
I still remember the snacks I ate around that time.

examples.ko: 친구는 작년 가을에 취직했어요. 저도 고맘때에는 꼭 취직하고 싶어요.
examples.en: My friend got a job last fall. I really want to have a job by around that time too.

explain: 지나간 때나 나이를 가리키며 '그맘때'가 더 흔해요. '고맘때'는 같은 뜻으로 쓰지만 조금 더 가볍고 귀엽게 들려요. 가까운 때를 말하는 '이맘때'와 짝으로 기억하세요.
explain_en: It points to a time or age already mentioned, and '그맘때' is more common. '고맘때' has the same meaning but sounds a little lighter and cuter. Remember it as a pair with '이맘때' (around this time).

examples.ko: 마을 입구에 백 년 된 고목이 서 있어요.
examples.en: A hundred-year-old tree stands at the entrance to the village.
The grandmothers are resting under the old tree.
The old tree fell in the typhoon and blocked the road.
This old tree turns yellow every autumn.
I want to become a reliable person like an old tree.
A bird built a nest in the old tree.

explain: '고목나무'라고도 하지만 대화에서는 그냥 '고목'이라고 해요. 마을을 지켜 온 오래된 나무처럼 존경하는 느낌으로 많이 쓰고, 힘이 빠진 모습을 비유할 때도 있어요.
explain_en: People also say '고목나무', but in conversation plain '고목' is enough. It is often used with a respectful feeling for an old tree that has watched over a village, and sometimes as a metaphor for someone who has lost strength.

examples.ko: 올해 수출이 늘어난 것은 고무적인 일이에요.
examples.en: It is encouraging that exports grew this year.

examples.ko: 첫 시험에서 이런 결과가 나온 건 고무적이에요.
examples.en: It is encouraging to get this result on the first test.
Encouraging news came in, and everyone was happy.

examples.ko: 환자의 상태가 좋아지고 있어서 아주 고무적이에요.
examples.en: The patient is getting better, which is very encouraging.

examples.ko: 참가자가 작년보다 두 배 늘어난 건 고무적이라고 생각해요.
examples.en: I think it is encouraging that participants doubled from last year.

examples.ko: 이번 발표는 학생들에게 고무적인 신호가 됐어요.
examples.en: This announcement became an encouraging sign for the students.

explain: '희망적이다'와 비슷하지만 좀 더 격식 있고 뉴스나 발표에서 많이 나와요. 보통 '고무적이다', '고무적인 일'처럼 써요. 친구와 가볍게 말할 때는 '다행이다', '희망이 보이다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is close to '희망적이다' (hopeful) but more formal, and it often appears in news and presentations. It is usually used as '고무적이다' or '고무적인 일'. In casual talk with friends, people say '다행이다' or '희망이 보이다'.

examples.ko: 도서관의 오래된 고문서는 열람이 제한돼 있어요.
examples.en: Access to the old documents in the library is restricted.

examples.ko: 창고에 처박혀 있던 고문서 더미를 찾아냈어요.
examples.en: I found a pile of old documents that had been shoved away in a storage room.

examples.ko: 박물관에서 조선 시대 고문서 전시를 해요.
examples.en: The museum is holding an exhibition of Joseon-era documents.
I discovered an old document at my grandfather's house.
To read ancient documents, you need to know Chinese characters.

examples.ko: 고문서는 종이가 약해서 조심해서 다뤄야 해요.
examples.en: Ancient documents have fragile paper, so you must handle them carefully.

explain: 옛날에 쓴 편지, 계약서, 기록 같은 문서를 가리켜서 책을 말하는 '고서'와는 달라요. 박물관, 도서관, 역사 수업에서 많이 나와요. '고문서를 보관하다', '고문서를 해독하다'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: It refers to old letters, contracts and records, which is different from '고서' (old books). It comes up often in museums, libraries and history classes. Common patterns are '고문서를 보관하다' (keep) and '고문서를 해독하다' (decipher).

examples.en: The library is storing ancient writings digitally.
I met a professor who studies ancient literature.

examples.ko: 이 약초는 여러 고문헌에 기록돼 있어요.
examples.en: This herb is recorded in several ancient texts.

examples.ko: 고문헌 속 요리법을 다시 만들어 봤어요.
examples.en: I tried making a recipe from an ancient text.

examples.ko: 고문헌을 번역하는 일은 시간이 오래 걸려요.
examples.en: Translating ancient texts takes a long time.
The school museum has many precious ancient texts.

explain: 연구나 자료 이야기에서 '고문헌 연구', '고문헌 기록'처럼 주로 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '옛날 책', '옛 기록'이라고 해요. '고문헌에 따르면'은 근거를 말할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
explain_en: It mostly appears in research and source talk, as in '고문헌 연구' and '고문헌 기록'. In daily conversation people say '옛날 책' or '옛 기록'. '고문헌에 따르면' (according to ancient texts) is used when giving evidence.

examples.en: The accuser was questioned at the police station.

examples.ko: 이 사건의 고발인이 누구인지 알려지지 않았어요.
examples.en: It is not known who reported this case.
They keep the accuser's name secret.

examples.ko: 회사의 문제를 알린 고발인이 증언하러 나왔어요.
examples.en: The whistle-blower who exposed the company's problems came out to testify.

examples.ko: 고발인이 낸 자료가 큰 도움이 됐어요.
examples.en: The materials the accuser submitted were a great help.
The accuser came to court in person and spoke.

explain: 뉴스와 법 이야기에 나오는 말이에요. '고소인'은 피해를 입은 사람이 처벌을 원할 때 쓰고, '고발인'은 피해자가 아니어도 범죄를 알린 사람이에요. 일상에서는 '신고한 사람'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It appears in news and legal topics. '고소인' is a victim who wants punishment, while '고발인' can be someone who is not the victim but reports a crime. In daily speech people say '신고한 사람' (the person who reported it).

examples.ko: 시민 단체가 회사를 상대로 고발장을 냈어요.
examples.en: A civic group filed a complaint against the company.

examples.ko: 고발장에는 사건의 내용이 자세히 적혀 있었어요.
examples.en: The details of the case were written in the complaint.
The police received the complaint and began an investigation.
I consulted a lawyer before writing the complaint.
There was news that a complaint had been filed.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 고발장을 직접 들고 경찰서에 갔어요.
examples.en: He carried the complaint to the police station himself.

explain: '고발장을 내다', '고발장을 접수하다'처럼 써요. 피해자가 직접 내는 '고소장'과는 달라요. 일상에서는 '신고서'와 헷갈리지 말고, 범죄를 알리는 공식 문서에만 써요.
explain_en: It is used as '고발장을 내다' (file) or '고발장을 접수하다' (accept). It differs from '고소장', which the victim files. Do not confuse it with a general '신고서' (report form); it is only for official documents reporting a crime.

examples.en: When the mother-in-law and daughter-in-law get along, the home is peaceful.
There are many dramas about conflict between mothers-in-law and daughters-in-law.
My mother-in-law and I get along like friends.
Even between a mother-in-law and daughter-in-law, mutual respect is needed.
On holidays, the mother-in-law and daughter-in-law cook together.
Conversation is important for a mother-in-law and daughter-in-law to grow closer.

explain: 시어머니와 며느리 사이를 말해요. '고부 갈등'처럼 '고부'만 쓰기도 해요. '부자간', '모녀간'처럼 사람 사이를 나타내는 '-간'과 같은 짝이에요.
explain_en: It refers to the relationship between a mother-in-law and her daughter-in-law. People also say just '고부', as in '고부 갈등'. The '-간' ending works like in '부자간' (father and son) and '모녀간' (mother and daughter).

examples.en: The child listened obediently today.
My younger sibling answers meekly in front of Mom.

examples.ko: 고분고분 따르지 않고 자기 의견을 말했어요.
examples.en: He did not just go along meekly and stated his own opinion.

examples.ko: 그 강아지는 훈련사의 말을 고분고분 따라요.
examples.en: That puppy follows the trainer's words obediently.

examples.ko: 신입 사원이 고분고분 인사하고 자리에 앉았어요.
examples.en: The new employee greeted everyone politely and sat down.
It is boring if you just do everything you are told without question.

explain: 말을 거스르지 않고 순하게 따르는 모습에 써요. 어른이나 윗사람 앞에서 쓸 때가 많아요. 칭찬일 때도 있지만 '자기 생각이 없다'는 느낌이 될 수도 있어요.
explain_en: It describes following someone's words gently without resisting, often in front of elders or superiors. It can be praise, but sometimes it suggests the person has no opinions of their own.

examples.en: Our puppy is really obedient.
I was surprised that my daughter was so well-behaved today.
The teacher likes him because he is an obedient student.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 윗사람 앞에서 늘 고분고분해요.
examples.en: He is always meek in front of his superiors.
Since I apologized meekly, Mom let go of her anger too.
You do not always have to be obedient.

explain: '고분고분한 아이', '고분고분하게'처럼 활용해요. 반대로 말을 안 들을 때는 '고분고분하지 않다'라고 해요. 사람이나 동물의 성격과 태도를 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: It conjugates like '고분고분한 아이' (an obedient child) and '고분고분하게' (obediently). For the opposite, say '고분고분하지 않다' (not obedient). It describes the temperament or attitude of a person or animal.

examples.en: Do you know the origin of this idiom?
Many Chinese-character idioms appear on the exam.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 말씀하실 때 고사성어를 자주 쓰세요.
examples.en: My grandfather often uses idioms when he speaks.

examples.ko: 오늘 수업에서 새로운 고사성어 세 개를 배웠어요.
examples.en: In class today I learned three new idioms.
If you know idioms, it is easier to understand writing.
Idioms like these carry old stories inside them.

explain: 옛이야기에서 나온 말이라 '사자성어'와 조금 달라요. 보통 한자 네 글자로 되어 있지만 이야기가 있는 말을 가리켜요. 글이나 말에 넣으면 점잖고 지식 있는 느낌이 나요.
explain_en: It differs a bit from '사자성어' (four-character phrase) because it comes from an old story. It is usually four Chinese characters, but refers to one with a story behind it. Using one in speech or writing gives a polished, learned feeling.

examples.ko: 고사장에 들어갈 때 수험표를 꼭 보여 주세요.
examples.en: Please be sure to show your exam admission ticket when entering the exam hall.

examples.ko: 고사장이 집에서 너무 멀어서 일찍 출발했어요.
examples.en: The exam site was so far from home that I left early.

examples.ko: 시험 전날 고사장을 미리 확인해 두었어요.
examples.en: I checked the exam site in advance the day before the test.
My friends cheered me on in front of the exam hall.
You must keep your phone turned off in the exam hall.
The exam site is decided differently by each school.

explain: 큰 시험을 볼 때 시험을 치르는 장소를 가리켜요. '시험장'이라고도 하고, 수능이나 자격시험 안내문에서 자주 보여요. 보통 '고사장 안내', '고사장 입실'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It means the place where a big exam is taken. People also say '시험장', and it appears often in notices for the CSAT or certification exams. It is typically used as '고사장 안내' (site guide) or '고사장 입실' (entering the hall).

examples.en: I got altitude sickness while climbing the mountain.

examples.ko: 고산병이 오면 머리가 아프고 숨이 차요.
examples.en: When altitude sickness hits, you get a headache and shortness of breath.
To prevent altitude sickness, you have to climb slowly.

examples.ko: 티베트에 가기 전에 고산병 약을 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought altitude sickness medicine before going to Tibet.
Because of altitude sickness, I rested at the hotel on the first day.

examples.ko: 저는 높은 곳에 가도 고산병이 없어요.
examples.en: I do not get altitude sickness even at high places.

explain: 높은 곳에서 산소가 적어서 생기는 증상을 말해요. '고산병에 걸리다', '고산병이 오다'처럼 써요. 여행 이야기에서 자주 나오고, 약이나 준비물과 같이 말하는 일이 많아요.
explain_en: It refers to symptoms caused by low oxygen at high places. It is used as '고산병에 걸리다' (get it) or '고산병이 오다' (it hits). It comes up often in travel talk, together with medicine and preparation.

examples.ko: 우리 부모님은 젊을 때 고생고생하며 사셨어요.
examples.en: My parents lived through many hardships when they were young.
I had a really hard time all week because of moving.

examples.ko: 그 길을 찾느라 고생고생해서 겨우 도착했어요.
examples.en: I struggled so much to find the way that I barely arrived.
I am thankful to my mother, who went through so much raising children.
I have so much luggage that I am struggling on the stairs.
After going through so much hardship, I finally passed.

explain: '고생하다'를 반복해서 힘든 일을 오래, 많이 겪었다는 느낌을 더해요. 하소연하거나 지난 일을 이야기할 때 잘 어울려요. 윗사람에게는 '고생고생하시다'처럼 높여요.
explain_en: It repeats '고생하다' to add the feeling of having gone through hard things for a long time. It fits venting or telling stories about the past. For elders, make it honorific like '고생고생하시다'.

examples.en: In the Paleozoic era, trilobites lived in the sea.
The era after the Paleozoic is the Mesozoic.
I looked at Paleozoic fossils at the museum.

examples.ko: 고생대 말에 큰 변화가 있었다고 배웠어요.
examples.en: I learned that there was a big change at the end of the Paleozoic.
They say this rock was formed in the Paleozoic era.
In science class we compared the Paleozoic and Mesozoic eras.

explain: 지구의 역사를 나눌 때 쓰는 말로 '고생대, 중생대, 신생대' 순서로 외우면 쉬워요. 학교 과학 시간이나 박물관에서 많이 나와요. 보통 '고생대에는', '고생대 화석'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is used to divide Earth's history, and it is easy to remember in the order 고생대, 중생대, 신생대 (Paleozoic, Mesozoic, Cenozoic). It appears often in school science classes and museums. It is usually used as '고생대에는' or '고생대 화석'.
